concepts.title: Nature of Services: Intangibility and Inseparability

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Nature of Services: Intangibility and Inseparability' refers to.
questions.a: Services are intangible activities that cannot be stored, touched or separated from their provider, differ from goods on intangibility, inconsistency, inseparability, inventory loss and customer involvement, and banking, insurance, transport, warehousing and communication are the major business services.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Nature of Services: Intangibility and Inseparability'.
questions.a: A service is performed rather than produced, its quality varies by provider and situation, and it cannot be inventoried for later sale.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Nature of Services: Intangibility and Inseparability' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Business services (source: kebs104.txt nature of services section)

concepts.title: Banking: Types of Banks and Types of Accounts

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Banking: Types of Banks and Types of Accounts' refers to.
questions.a: A bank accepts deposits repayable on demand and lends the money, and its types include commercial banks, cooperative banks, central bank and specialised banks, while depositors may hold savings, current, fixed or recurring deposit accounts.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Banking: Types of Banks and Types of Accounts'.
questions.a: Banks create credit through lending, act as agents for collection and payment, and the Reserve Bank of India supervises them as the central bank.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Banking: Types of Banks and Types of Accounts' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Insurance: Principles and Types' refers to.
questions.a: Insurance is a contract in which the insurer indemnifies the insured against a specified loss in return for premium, resting on principles of utmost good faith, insurable interest, indemnity, contribution, subrogation, mitigation and cause proxima.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Insurance: Principles and Types'.
questions.a: Life insurance, fire insurance and marine insurance differ in the nature of risk covered, and the premium is the consideration paid by the insured for the cover.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Insurance: Principles and Types' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Transport, Warehousing, Communication and Postal Services

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Transport, Warehousing, Communication and Postal Services' refers to.
questions.a: Transport removes the hindrance of place by carrying goods by road, rail, air or waterways, warehousing removes the hindrance of time by storing goods till demand arises, and communication and postal services link buyers and sellers by moving information.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Transport, Warehousing, Communication and Postal Services'.
questions.a: Warehouses may be private, public, bonded or government, and bonded warehouses let importers store goods until customs duty is paid.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Transport, Warehousing, Communication and Postal Services' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Transport and warehousing (source: kebs104.txt transport and warehousing sections)
